about: The frame every editing skill lays a reel out on. Positions are on the 1080x1920 grid: double them for a 2160x3840 export. charles-claude-editing owns these numbers. Every other editing skill ships an identical copy of this file, and the repository's scripts/check.mjs fails when a copy differs.

platform.why: Instagram and TikTok draw their header above y 200, the username, post caption and audio below y 1500, and the like, comment and share column right of x 940 from y 840 down. Footage and pictures may run under all three. Words, faces that matter and anything else the viewer must see never do.

text_inset.why: Text stays 60 px inside each side of the frame, and 60 px inside every edge of a slot (a card, a split panel), so a phone's rounded corners and the platform's chrome never touch it.

bands.why: A hook title, a hero number or a section word sits in the headline band, and the one focal object in the subject band. The caption band belongs to the captions: while one is up, nothing the viewer must read, and nothing bright, crosses it.

captions.why: Talking-head reels centre their captions at y 1380, inside the caption band. On a split screen they sit on the seam instead. A full 3D reel draws its own captions lower in the same band (charles-3d-explainers).

slots.why: The five sizes charles-claude-editing asks the visual skills for. A card is rendered larger than it shows (a 1280x630 card shows about 900x442) so its small text stays sharp.

pacing.why: While he talks, something on screen changes every 2-3 s and never more than 4 s apart, one change at a time and at least 0.5 s apart, except a run of quick cuts where how many is the point. A still stays up 3 s at most unless he is reading it out or it is the payoff. A layout that covers his face comes off within about 2 s for the same reasons.

audio.why: His voice is levelled with gain only to -16 LUFS over the samples where he speaks. The music sits 8-9 dB under it with no sidechain ducking, because his pauses are too short to duck in and out of and harder ducking makes the voice sound isolated. The finished mix is brought to -14 LUFS with a look-ahead peak limiter.

export.why: Small text anywhere on screen (a UI, code, a tweet, a screenshot) means a 2160x3840 export: at 1080 wide, 10 px UI text goes soft once the phone scales it up. A talking head with only captions and a hook can stay 1080x1920.
